Follow the commit-message skill guidelines from SKILL.md. Write a clear, well-structured commit message using the canonical format (not conventional commits).

Requirements:
- Subject line ≤ 50 characters, no ending period
- Blank line after subject
- Body wrapped at 72 characters
- Lead with most important information (pyramid structure)
- Explain the "why" not just the "what"
- Appropriate detail level for change complexity
- Self-contained (understandable without external resources)

Output only the commit message, nothing else.

This is an exemplary commit message that demonstrates best practices across all criteria.

response.output:
Handle deleted payment methods in refund flow

Refunds were crashing when users had deleted their payment methods
after making a purchase. The code assumed the payment method would
always exist in the database, causing null reference errors when
accessing the token property.

Add a null check for the payment method lookup. When the payment
method has been deleted, fall back to using the cached payment token
and currency stored on the order record. This data is captured at
purchase time and persists even after users delete their payment
methods.

This ensures refunds complete successfully regardless of whether
users have cleaned up their stored payment methods.
